On the 1500 map, Islamic states covers the lower Indus and the dry mountains to its west, today's Sindh and Balochistan in Pakistan, then shared among several Muslim rulers.

In Sindh the Sammas ruled from Thatta; see Sind. North along the Indus, the Langah Sultanate held Multan. The hills and deserts to the west were the land of Baloch tribes, whose chiefs owed loose loyalty to whoever was strongest, and of the Brahui of Kalat.

Larger powers pressed on all sides. The Timurid princes of Herat and Kandahar were losing ground, and in 1501 the Safavids began their rise in Iran. Driven from Kandahar by Babur, the Arghun family turned south and took Sindh in 1520. A generation later the region fell between Mughal India and Safavid Iran.
sum: On the 1500 map, Islamic states covers the lower Indus and the dry mountains to its west, today's Sindh and Balochistan in Pakistan, then shared among several Muslim rulers.
